Gold broke below 3,553.00. This morning I'm watching where the rebound stops, up to the daily open.

As of 06:53 on Nov 25, XS's MT5 (XAUUSDs) is at 3,554.10. Today's low is 3,546.66, which briefly went below the previous day's low of 3,553.00. The current price is slightly above the previous day's low. On TradingView, the band between the previous day's low and the round number 3,550.00 is the first zone to check on the 1-hour chart.

[If it returns upward]
If the 1-hour close stays above 3,553.00, the next zone is 3,600.00 and the 4-hour SMA20 at 3,601.91. I watch whether price is pushed back there or stays above. If it holds beyond that zone, the daily open of 3,637.15 is the next target, since it makes it easy to compare in the daily body how much of this morning's drop was recovered.

[If it extends downward]
If the 1-hour closes below 3,550.00 and below today's and this week's low of 3,546.66, next I watch the 4-hour trough at 3,502.78 and the round number 3,500.00. I'll log separately in my verification notes cases where a wick goes below today's low but price recovers by the close, versus closing outside the low.

On the 4-hour chart SMA20 is below SMA50 at 3,740.52, and the snapshot price is below SMA20. I use this alignment as background, and record how close the rebound reached the previous day's low. When reviewing later, pairing the reached zone with the 1-hour close position makes it easier to compare where momentum faded even for the same "rebound".

Trade at your own judgment. Views on each zone and verification notes are shared in the open chat "Hide Gold FX Study Group" in my profile.

[On overseas FX deposit/withdrawal regulation]

Many of you may be worried, but let's first understand it correctly.

The focus of this regulation is not "overseas FX itself" but the "payment agents".

It is not illegal for Japanese residents to use overseas FX and make deposits and withdrawals.

■ About bank deposits/withdrawals

- It doesn't look like bank deposits/withdrawals will suddenly all become unusable.
- You may be asked to confirm transaction details and the source of funds.
(As mentioned before, overseas FX is not illegal)
- Depending on the bank, account restrictions or freezes are possible.

Even if an account is frozen, your funds are not confiscated. However, confirmation and release may take time.

I recommend separating your main bank used for living expenses and salary from the bank account used for overseas FX.

■ About crypto deposits/withdrawals

Each broker recommends using crypto for deposits and withdrawals.

From now on, it is good to understand crypto deposit/withdrawal methods rather than relying only on bank transfers.
I will put together the crypto deposit/withdrawal flow later.

■ About credit cards

They remain available.

However, in some cases withdrawals are made by bank transfer rather than refunded to the card, so check each broker's deposit/withdrawal rules in advance.

■ Summary

This regulation does not prohibit the use of overseas FX.

What matters is:

- Secure multiple deposit/withdrawal methods
- Separate living-expense and trading accounts
- Keep transaction history and deposit/withdrawal records

There's no need to be overly anxious.

It's important to understand correct information and adapt to changes in the environment.

That said, this is only my personal opinion at this point. I'm also in talks with each broker, so let's keep updating with the latest information.
